Thanks for pointing this out. I believe #46527 is related to #44821, but it proposes a narrower and different change.

#44821 investigates the physical maximum input accepted by the OAuth endpoint and discusses dynamic or override-based limit resolution. This request does not attempt to determine or expose that physical endpoint maximum.

Instead, it proposes exposing the opt-in long-context tier already defined by Codex itself:

- The bundled GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna metadata uses `context_window: 272000` and `max_context_window: 872000`.
- Codex has a test confirming that setting `model_context_window` to `1_000_000` resolves these three models to `872_000`.

Sources:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6be2a6ca952ac9f70676ce4dd07fda27175aa9dd/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json#L30-L31
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6be2a6ca952ac9f70676ce4dd07fda27175aa9dd/codex-rs/models-manager/src/manager_tests.rs#L731-L751
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6be2a6ca952ac9f70676ce4dd07fda27175aa9dd/codex-rs/models-manager/src/model_info.rs#L25-L33

OpenCode currently exposes only the conservative OAuth limits. #46527 proposes mirroring Codex's two-tier behavior:

- keep the existing 272K input budget as the default;
- add an explicit opt-in model entry using a 1M total context budget, with 872K input and 128K output;
- leave API-key authentication and existing defaults unchanged.

Therefore, #44821 addresses the broader endpoint-capacity and dynamic-resolution problem, while #46527 proposes a specific selectable model-catalog feature based on Codex's existing long-context ceiling.

## Update: crash reproduces without /compact

The same `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` crash just happened again **without running `/compact`**. The process ran for ~19 minutes and crashed on its own.

### New crash report

- `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/opencode.exe-2026-09-01-094317.ips`
- Incident ID: `C8F5FA18-EBC8-473D-8264-465B48E14C2E`

### Key details

```
exception: EXC_BREAKPOINT (signal SIGTRAP, code 5)
faultingThread: 9 (named "Worker")
uptime: 16000ms
procLaunch: 2026-09-01 09:24:23
captureTime: 2026-09-01 09:43:16
```

Same crash signature — `EXC_BREAKPOINT`, PAC trap on a Worker thread, in opencode's own binary. This time the process lived ~19 minutes before crashing, with no manual `/compact` invocation. The crash is not specific to compaction — it's a general worker thread assertion failure that `/compact` was merely triggering faster.

The process was consuming ~4.6 GB of memory before the crash, which may be related to the trigger condition.

Independent reproduction on **1.18.15** (released build, macOS 26.6.2 arm64), with a datapoint the thread does not have yet: **this reproduces even when the two roots are the same directory.**

I consolidated my hubs down to one, expecting that to fix it:

```
~/.agents/skills            REAL (13 skills)
~/.claude/skills         -> ~/.agents/skills   (root-level symlink)
~/.config/opencode/skills   removed
```

There is now exactly one real skills directory on disk. It still fails, because discovery globs `.claude` and `.agents` independently and the glob follows the symlinked root, so both phases still yield distinct absolute path strings for the same file.

Minimal fixture — two roots, one target, isolated `HOME`:

```
/tmp/globtest/home/.agents/skills -> /tmp/globtest/real
/tmp/globtest/home/.claude/skills -> /tmp/globtest/home/.agents/skills
```

```
WARN duplicate skill name name=one existing=.../.agents/skills/one/SKILL.md duplicate=.../.claude/skills/one/SKILL.md
WARN duplicate skill name name=two existing=.../.claude/skills/two/SKILL.md duplicate=.../.agents/skills/two/SKILL.md
```

Note `one` and `two` resolve from **opposite** roots within a single run.

Confirming @sergical's correction over "per process": on my real install (13 skills, ~28.3k-char system prompt, `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` via a LiteLLM gateway, captured on the wire by a proxy), 6 consecutive `opencode run` invocations gave:

```
distinct system-prompt hashes: 6 / 6
cache hits:                    0 / 6      (write=65490 every run, read=0 every run)
```

`sysLen` was identical (28351) in all six, so this is not content drift — only the `<location>` strings move. The `.claude`-vs-`.agents` split wandered per run: `claude=3,4,2,2,6,4` of 20 location lines. Deterministic ordering alone would fix it; byte-length stability means the prompt is otherwise stable.

Two practical notes for anyone landing a fix:

- `skills.paths` cannot be used as a workaround. It is additive (`skills?.paths ?? []` is iterated *after* the built-in roots), so it cannot suppress a hardcoded root. The roots are constants: `var bA=".claude", xA=".agents", GA="skills/**/SKILL.md"`.
- The only configuration I found that yields 0 duplicates is `~/.claude/skills` not existing — which is not viable for anyone also running Claude Code, since it has no configurable skills location.

Dedupe by resolved realpath (rather than path string) would additionally cover the symlinked-root case above, which basename dedupe alone handles only incidentally.

The `opencode upgrade` scoop-vs-npm mixup is the install-detection code, your exec path sits under `C:\Users\...\scoop\` so the scoop branch wins the sort, and `scoop list opencode` always prints that 'Installed apps matching' header, which is why the includes check never catches it. Workaround until it's patched: skip the built-in updater and run `npm install -g opencode-ai@<version>` yourself, or patch installation/index.ts to prefer npm whenever `npm list -g --depth=0` shows opencode-ai. Fixed the same mess on my Windows box that way.

Following up on this thread since the two plugin solutions posted earlier are no longer maintained: @mattaschmann's [opencode-model-alias](https://github.com/mattaschmann/opencode-model-alias) was unpublished from npm in June, and @krystofrezac's gist hasn't been updated since April.

I've forked and substantially hardened Matt's plugin — it's now published as **[`@renaudcerrato/opencode-model-alias`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@renaudcerrato/opencode-model-alias)** (MIT, 182 tests / 100% coverage). It covers the exact workflow requested here: define aliases like `cheap`/`smart` in `~/.config/opencode/model-aliases.json`, reference them in any agent/command `model` field, and remap per machine without touching shared configs. It also adds model variants and alias chains (stable role names layered on machine-specific mappings).

Setup is just a config entry — opencode installs npm plugins automatically:
```json
{ "plugin": ["@renaudcerrato/opencode-model-alias@1.1.2"] }
```

If native support ever lands (the closed PR #11352 was a step in that direction), the plugin becomes unnecessary — until then this fills the gap.
